record_notes.DCP-LETT-1365: 10, supplied September 1853 ALS. Two blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Uncertain recollection of Lubbock oral mention of Pycnogon metamorphosis prompts reference request for Bate. Matches missing-reference discussion in own 1528, not an incoming Lubbock letter. Quatrefages identification in apparatus and possible later Dana work sent to Bate distinct; Darwin does not yet know exact paper here. Sowerby work exhausting, later payment totals not current new knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1585: Thursday in supplied September 1854, not a unique day. Four blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Sends unidentified beetle, qualifies 26-year memory. Westwood reading has revived interest, own copy now ordered, not necessarily delivered or entire work finished. September 25 reading log is separately dated; cannot map uncertain Thursday automatically before or after it. Cambridge drinking reminiscence and explicit present no wine remain source humor, not current intoxication claim.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1673: April 24, supplied 1855 ALS. Six blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Manuscript read sufficiently to offer no corrections, expected Annals destination not actual later Transactions publication. Lubbock work and invitations acknowledged, fresh-water molluscs sought for existing small vivarium but not received. Experiment aim salt-water survival appears in apparatus, not completed result in body. No source-complete manuscript/cover note preserved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1831: 14, supplied July 1855 ALS corroborated by dinner itinerary. Five blocks and five footnotes. Sufficient Helix pomatia acquired yesterday, July 13, no assertion Lubbock supplied these particular specimens. Lepidoptera books received and boys studying, not proof Darwin completed them. Larch wood about 115 species collected, acreage and planting date still unknown. Horner visit and Tuesday dinner prospective; later July 17 event corroborates date without proving invited Lubbock attended.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1720: 19, supplied July 1855 ALS. Five blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Missing Lyell note received this morning reports fossil Ovibos discovery, not direct Lubbock incoming. Darwin geological interpretation contemporary; 1856 Owen description and later publications excluded from current knowledge. June 16 Lyell-to-Lubbock letter cited in apparatus is a distinct correspondence witness, not this missing July 19-arrived Lyell note. P4 confirms Lubbock missed Tuesday invitation, contrasting earlier plan 1831.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1751: August 31, supplied 1855 ALS. Four blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Tegetmeier offer of carcasses known but mode not fixed by body; enclosed desired-birds list missing. Only few hoped for, expense reimbursement offered, future London visit and Journal gift conditional. Retrospective first-meeting recollection conflicts with likely Anerley context; do not invent exact first meeting or preserved offer wording. No birds received here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1754: Thursday supplied September 13, 1855 at Glasgow association meeting. Four blocks, six footnotes and bibliography. Tegetmeier note forwarded and received, pamphlet explicitly not forwarded; only supposes it at home. No reading of pamphlet implied by later inscribed copy or quoted pamphlet apparatus. Fox Dorking only promised; Darwin revises belief white type differed only in colour. Selective desired breeds broadened; existing pigeons observed, not all newly offered breeds received. Journal gift on return prospective. Apparatus end-of-April house completion exceeds 1660 April 25 nearly-complete body; preserve respective scope.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1782: November 16, supplied 1855 ALS. Both blocks, footnote and bibliography. Requests Friday visit after next Thursday London travel, conditional on reply and train timetable not known because Bradshaw lost. No completed visit yet. Tegetmeier later album calls this first letter and Thursday meeting, while actual earlier correspondence exists and body requests Friday; retain retrospective discrepancy, not silent substitution.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1788: Sunday evening supplied December 2, 1855 by endorsement. Seven blocks, six footnotes, bibliography and raw numeric markup read. Visit occurred, skull discussed but canine length not measured then; now asks gum-exposed and full lengths, colour/size unknown. Raw HTML 1100 with superscript th lacks fraction markup; intended one-hundredth rendering held. Ordered pigeons distinct from two ducks actually brought home. Rare carcasses future if birds die, not current possession. Prepared hen skull given, white Poland identity only presumed and queried; H pencil label Darwin own. Later Variation .95/.6 dimensions not available in this letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1791: December 6, supplied 1855 ALS. Four blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Answers received but cat canines only sent and hoped to arrive safely, not yet proven receipt. Four cat variations gathered over six weeks, not uniform experiment. Recognizes Tegetmeier own need for Ghoondok, waives manuscript account in favour of future print; later skeleton loan conditional. Wild Indian jungle-fowl head/skeleton already in Darwin possession by offer, separately related to Blyth shipment; exact arrival and Blyth letter receipt not established here. Postscript notices to Gardeners Chronicle described as trifles, not absent publication.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1464: December 19 in mutually exclusive 1852 OR 1854, unknown recipient. Two blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Missing note dated 16th acknowledged, no exact receipt. Twenty-two copies received, not simply twenty; apparatus suggests author plus subscription copies, not proven explanation. Published volume number cannot be uniquely fixed from editorial summary. Price inquiry for possible sale, not purchased copy. No inferred Lankester identity.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13872: December 31 in mutually exclusive 1852 OR 1853; unknown recipient. Four blocks, seven footnotes and bibliography. Coquimbo shell discussion cites own book and distinguishes Sowerby, d Orbigny and own species judgments. Bed age Miocene or Eocene explicitly uncertain; genus and species criteria differ. Period assignment inferred from no reference to 1854 cirripede volume, not independently exact year. Modern synonyms and later classifications remain apparatus. Missing request not inferred from generic scientific topic.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1578A: August 16 in one of 1854–1858 inclusive, five discrete alternatives; unknown recipient and source carrier unspecified in XML. One full block, footnote and bibliography. Dating based on completed work and other natural-history occupation, not uniquely proved year. Some alternatives outside this review period, all before Origin cutoff; hold period/date and recipient.

Specimens unspecified, possibly bats only in apparatus from later 1860 retrospective letter, not certain current request. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1746: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Complete August 22–23, 1855 composite letter and accompanying miscellaneous memorandum read, sixteen extracted blocks, twenty footnotes, annotation and bibliography. P1 has already dispatched then recalled memoranda on receiving Hutton answers; this proves Blyth access to Hutton, not Darwin receipt. P2–6 quoted Hutton observations interspersed with Blyth qualifications; paragraph-level single-speaker labels would misattribute comments. P3 raw 50/- (£5) preserved as source notation without automatic currency correction; interpretation not verified. P7 future Burma/Ceylon notes not received observations. P8 merges closing Blyth signature, Miscellaneous Notes heading, and cat note inside one extraction block; retain internal boundaries. P8–14 enclosure topics and prospective photographs; August 23 dated closing at P15, P16 subsequent P.S. Opening August 22 versus enclosure closing August 23 remains separate; recalled-dispatch story and editorial ordering do not justify an exact reconstructed physical sequence or a single earlier timestamp for whole source. Rüppell travels explicitly never seen (P10), despite consulted Systematische uebersicht; observed Afghan moths not minutely compared (P9); canary cross is inquiry, not confirmed identity. Photography planned next week; wife current daguerreotype work separate. P16 jungle-fowl expected with this mail is prospective and later than August 4 promise; no exact arrival or reading. Future 1860 handwriting comment, later taxonomy and 1867 donation remain apparatus, not contemporaneous knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1528: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. August 30, supplied 1853 ALS. reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
